text:

   URL: https://simonucl.github.io/blog/2026/scope/

query: adaptive user simulator reward design LLM agents
text:
1. **Learning User Simulators with Turing Rewards** — The closest match. Introduces Turing-RL, where an LLM judge supplies an “indistinguishability” reward for training user simulators. Yingshan Susan Wang, Cedegao E. Zhang, Linlu Qiu, Zexue He, Pengyuan Li, Alex Pentland, Roger P. Levy, and Yoon Kim — **MIT and Stanford University**.  
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19336

2. **Quantifying the Utility of User Simulators for Building Collaborative LLM Assistants** — Compares role-playing and human-grounded simulators by measuring the real-user performance of assistants trained against them. Joseph Suh, Ayush Raj, Minwoo Kang, and Serina Chang — **UC Berkeley / Berkeley AI Research**.  
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09808

3. **Reward Design with Language Models** — Uses prompted LLMs as proxy reward functions for training RL agents according to natural-language user objectives. Minae Kwon, Sang Michael Xie, and Dorsa Sadigh — **Stanford University**; Kalesha Bullard — **DeepMind**.  
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.00001

4. **User Behavior Simulation with Large Language Model-Based Agents** — Builds profile-, memory-, and action-based LLM agents inside a sandbox for simulating user behavior and social dynamics. Lei Wang, Jingsen Zhang, Hao Yang, Zhi-Yuan Chen, Jiakai Tang, Zeyu Zhang, Xu Chen, Yankai Lin, Hao Sun, Ruihua Song, Wayne Xin Zhao, Jun Xu, Zhicheng Dou, and Ji-Rong Wen — **Renmin University of China / Beijing Key Laboratory of Big Data Management and Analysis Methods**; Jun Wang — **University College London**.  
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02552

5. **Mock Worlds, Real Skills: Building Small Agentic Language Models with Synthetic Tasks, Simulated Environments, and Rubric-Based Rewards** — SYNTHAGENT combines an LLM user simulator, mocked tool environments, underspecified tasks, and rubric-based rewards for agent training. Yuanjie Lyu, Chengyu Wang, Lei Shen, Jun Huang, and Tong Xu; affiliations are listed in the paper.  
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22511

query: within-run and across-run adaptation agent training
text:
1. **EAU: Environment–Agent–User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents** — The closest match: adapts the training system both intra-run through live hot-swaps and inter-run by preserving successful changes. People: Min Cai, Dan Zhang, Gao Xing, Libin Ma, Zhaohui Xu, Xi Ye. Affiliations: University of Alberta, Amii, National University of Singapore, Kuaishou Technology, and an independent researcher. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16523)

2. **ASCENT: Online Test-Time Training of Long-Horizon Agents via Self-Distillation of Verified Experience** — Updates an agent’s weights during deployment and carries those updates across subsequent tasks. People: Haodong Lu and Dong Gong. Affiliation: UNSW Sydney. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05303)

3. **Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation** — Trains a proposer to revise an agent’s executable harness from within-task execution feedback; learned revision behavior generalizes across tasks and supports successive adaptation rounds. People: Alvin Zhang, Xuecheng Liu, Zixuan Wang, Fahim Tajwar, Daman Arora, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, Daniel Khashabi, Yuda Song, Andrea Zanette. Affiliations: Carnegie Mellon University and Johns Hopkins University. [Paper page](https://huggingface.co/papers/2609.35738)

4. **Evo-Harness: Context-to-Harness Skill Compilation for Self-Evolving Agents** — Compiles lessons from individual executions into structured, reusable harness skills that improve a frozen agent across sequential tasks. People: Tianxin Wei, Zhan Shi, Minhua Lin, Bing He, Zewen Liu, Yisi Sang, Yuanchen Bei, Xuying Ning, Jiaru Zou, Ting-Wei Li, Xiao Lin, Yanjun Zhao, Chi Wang, Benoit Dumoulin, Dakuo Wang, Jingrui He, Hanqing Lu. Affiliations include UIUC, Amazon, Penn State, and Emory University. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15071)

query: LLM agent training environment evolves with policy
text:

query: multi-turn reinforcement learning user simulation benchmarks
text:
1. **LMRL Gym: Benchmarks for Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning with Language Models** — The closest direct match: eight interactive language tasks with online simulators and offline datasets for evaluating RL methods. People: Marwa Abdulhai, Isadora White, Charlie Snell, Charles Sun, Joey Hong, Yuexiang Zhai, Kelvin Xu, and Sergey Levine. Affiliations: UC Berkeley and Google DeepMind.  
   URL: https://lmrl-gym.github.io/

2. **UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning** — A framework of standardized gym environments, simulated users, and multi-turn GRPO training/evaluation. People: Cheng Qian, Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, Jielin Qiu, Zhiwei Liu, Haolin Chen, Shirley Kokane, Heng Ji, Weiran Yao, Shelby Heinecke, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, and Huan Wang.    URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.19736

3. **CustomerSim: Benchmarking and Aligning Multimodal Language Models as Retail User Simulators** — A 360-persona retail benchmark plus UserGRPO, a multi-turn, multi-objective RL method for improving simulated-user behavior. People: Yada Pruksachatkun, Yixin Wan, Xingrun Chen, Kai-Wei Chang, and Chien-Sheng Wu. Affiliations: Salesforce Research and UCLA.  
   URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.08334

4. **SimulatorArena: Are User Simulators Reliable Proxies for Multi-Turn Evaluation of AI Assistants?** — Benchmarks user simulators against 909 human–AI conversations in tutoring and document creation; especially relevant for validating simulators used in RL evaluation. People: Yao Dou, Michel Galley, Baolin Peng, Chris Kedzie, Weixin Cai, Alan Ritter, Chris Quirk, Wei Xu, and Jianfeng Gao. Affiliations: Georgia Institute of Technology and Microsoft.

5. **Consistently Simulating Human Personas with Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning** — Trains user simulators with PPO and turn-level consistency rewards across multi-turn dialogue trajectories. query: methods improving user-centric agents with simulated users
text:
1. **UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agents via Reinforcement Learning** — Trains agents through multi-turn reinforcement learning against simulated users; emphasizes reward shaping, trajectory scoring, and simulator choice. People: Cheng Qian and Heng Ji (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign); Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, Jielin Qiu, Zhiwei Liu, Haolin Chen, Shirley Kokane, Weiran Yao, Shelby Heinecke, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, and Huan Wang (Salesforce AI Research). [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.19736)

2. **Training User Simulators with Latent Intrinsic Feedback** — Adds simulated internal thoughts, reactions, and ratings to user simulators, then uses those signals as rewards for training assistants. It reports comparable performance to external-judge rewards at less than half the RL compute. People: Tarek Naous and Wei Xu (Georgia Institute of Technology); Craig Boutilier and Ofer Meshi (Google DeepMind). [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13617)

3. **HumanLM: Simulating Users with State Alignment Beats Response Imitation** — Improves personalized user simulation by learning psychologically grounded latent states—such as beliefs and emotions—rather than merely copying response style. People: Shirley Wu, Evelyn Choi, Arpandeep Khatua, Joy He-Yueya, Tharindu Cyril Weerasooriya, Wei Wei, Diyi Yang, Jure Leskovec, and James Zou (Stanford University); Zhanghan Wang (University of Southern California). [Paper](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/wu26k.html)

4. **SimUser: Generating Usability Feedback by Simulating Various Users Interacting with Mobile Applications** — Uses paired application and user agents, persona characteristics, contextual factors, and structured reasoning to identify usability problems during prototyping. People: Wei Xiang, Hanfei Zhu, Suqi Lou, Xinli Chen, Zhenghua Pan, Yuping Jin, Shi Chen, and Lingyun Sun (Zhejiang University, principally its International Design Institute). [Paper](https://doi.org/10.1145/3613904.3642481)

5. **UXCascade: Scalable Usability Testing with Simulated User Agents** — Aggregates persona-based agents’ actions and think-aloud traces into UX patterns, concrete issues, proposed interface changes, and repeat simulations. People: Steffen Holter (ETH Zürich); Eunyee Koh, Mustafa Doga Dogan, and Gromit Yeuk-Yin Chan (Adobe Research). [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.15777)

6. **SAGE: A Top-Down Bottom-Up Knowledge-Grounded User Simulator for Multi-turn Agent Evaluation** — Combines top-down user attributes with bottom-up business knowledge—catalogs, FAQs, and knowledge bases—to generate realistic task scenarios and diagnose agent errors. [Paper](https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-eacl.147/)
